label: text
text: YOUNG LADY'S FLIGHT FROM CANTON.

label: text
text: TWO BOMBS FOUND.

label: text
text: Recalling to mind notorious residents of Occidental women's opinionage is a stirring report from an on of how a beautiful young lady spy barely escaped capture.

label: text
text: In such cases," the heroine is always described as "young" and "charming," who matter her real claims to loveliness. But the young woman in Canton went by a nickname which meant that she would have won the devotion of even a soulless Buddha!

label: text
text: Her activities were alleged to be on behalf of a "certain party," the name of which is not given. It must be presumed that her principles were alleged enemies of Canton.

label: text
text:
A detective got on her track and led a raid on a house in a fashionable district in Honam, the island suburb on the side of the river opposite to Canton.
But this young woman was too quick for them, fleeting. It is surprised, through a back door on the very approach of the posse of police.

label: text
text: A search is stated to have revealed two bombs of "egg shape," whatever that may mean. A quantity of documents found in the house gave away her identity and further developments are expected.

label: paragraph_title
text: CANTON'S WAR.

label: text
text: MANY PROVINCES JOINING IN FRAY?

label: text
text: IMPORTANT DESPATCHES.

label: text
text: From a batch of important despatches to hand, it is evident that Canton's allies still holding Changshu, a town in a strategic position in Central China, while Wu Pei-fu's faction are yet in possession of Yochow. The messages read:—

label: text
text: Governor Yang Sin of Szechuan province had instructed two generals to assist Hunan province (against the south?).

label: text
text: Twenty field pieces have been assembled at Yochow and the cruiser (or gunboat) "Yung Kien" is proceeding thither. An offensive (against the south) will be launched in a week.

label: text
text: Steps have been taken by ex-President Tsao Kun to ask Wu Pei-fu to return to the south. Wu replied that Canton's Northern Expedition is more in the shape of propaganda. His military and naval strength is converging in great number at Yochow and Sun Chuan-fang is assisting his campaign. When Nankow is taken (from the Christian general's former army) he will return to Hankow.

label: text
text: To assist Chao Hang-teh is restoring himself to the governorship of Hunan (as against Canton's nominee, Tang Sang-chee), Wu Pei-fu has allotted Chao $100,000 and Sun Chuan-fang (Tupan of Kiangsi) is remitting $50,000. Chao is waiting for the re-capture of Changsha before reassuming the governorship.

label: text
text: Wu Pei-fu has appointed a subordinate as commander of the Yangtsze Flotilla. He has ordered a general attack on Changsha.

label: text
text: Of Sun Chuan-fang's subordinates it is stated that he is sending a division and two autonomous brigades into Fukien (the province to the north of Kwangtung). His 76th brigade at Nantung is also ready to march. On August 2 Yang Wen-kai passed Hsuchow en route for Kiangsu province.

label: text
text: The gist of these reports is that activities are hinted, if not having actually taken place, by the various warlords whose domains are close to Canton's sphere. Meanwhile Canton is quiet about General Chang Kai-shek's taking the command in person but it is felt that far-reaching developments, with possible influence on the whole of South China, are imminent.

label: paragraph_title
text: CANTON'S STRIKES

label: text
text: The strikes of postmen and newspaper employees at Canton are not reported ended, nor is a settlement in sight, according to latest messages to hand.

label: text
text: There is no mention of the seamen and railwaymen coming out in sympathy.

label: paragraph_title
text: STREET DANGERS.

label: text
text: FIRE ENGINE DROPS IN A PIT

label: text
text: TWO HOURS' LABOUR

label: text
text: Following the usual custom, the engine turned round in front of the No. 2 Police Station on the return journey but one of the front wheels got stuck in a trench temporarily covered in with earth for the night.

label: text
text: The engine got clear by working on reverse gear, but must a worse fate, as the rear left hand wheel broke through some planking placed over a deep hole and fell in with a crash. The planks which were replaced over the pit as protection for the night collapsed owing to the weight of the fire appliance.

label: text
text: Assistance was summoned by telephone from the Central Fire Station and with the combined efforts of the firemen the engine was extricated about nearly two hours' work.

label: text
text: The mudguards of that portion of the appliance would have been smashed but for the fact that the ends also went into the pit and further progress was stopped by the ladders stays at the rear and the tool box fixed along the dashboard. There was little apparent damage and the appliance returned to the depot none the worse for the mishap.

label: text
text: Profiling by this experience, the pit was again closed with planks and two lanterns placed over it to warn traffic.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: POLICE COURT CASE.

label: text
text: With blood stains on his clothing and head "in bandages," a truck coolie looked on passively at the Central Magistracy this morning while another man explained from the dock the cause of the trouble.

label: text
text: The defendant, also a truck coolie, alleged that he was struck on the leg with a bamboo pole when he questioned complainant's right to precede him with a truck. He retaliated when another attack was premeditated.

label: text
text: Div.-Inspector Grant said that the defendant nursed a grievance and took the opportunity when he met complainant again in the afternoon to hit him on the head with a shovel.

label: text
text: Defendant was fined $5 and ordered to pay a like sum as compensation.

label: paragraph_title
text: TRAMWAY

label: text
text: EXPLANATIONS IN COURT.

label: text
text: Two Chinese, brothers, were brought before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning for an infringement of the Tramway Company's by-laws. One was charged with transferring his July monthly ticket to the younger boy and the latter with using a ticket not in his name.

label: text
text: The elder boy explained that he sent his brother to exchange his ticket for a new one, but Mr. A. Gillard, of the Tramway Company, mentioned that the ticket holder lived in Bonham Strand, and the boy was found on a car between Causeway Bay and Quarry Bay. Further, that the boy did not appear to have any money when brought to the depot.

label: text
text: The younger said that he wanted to watch the swimmers at the North Point beach first and when arrested he was too frightened to mention about the renewal of the ticket.

label: text
text: Each of the youths was ordered to pay a fine of $10.

label: text
text: BANKRUPTCY COURT.

label: text
text: Sir Henry Cowper Gollan, Chief Justice, sat in Bankruptcy jurisdiction this morning to try a partnership issue.

label: text
text:
Mr. H. G. Sheldon, appearing for Fook Tong, alias Wong Huen, a creditor of the Hing Loong Shing Kee, the debtor firm, said that the case had been adjourned from a previous hearing for notice of trial to be given and certain advertisements inserted. This order had been complied with.
The debtor firm (which dealt in salt fish) had been adjudicated bankrupt on June 5, said counsel, and later, in Chambers, His Lordship had made an order that the issue should be tried as to whether Chan Yuk-san was a partner in the debtor firm.

label: text
text: Evidence was called including that of the accountant of the debtor firm who said that Chan Yuk-san was in sole control of the business and had been so for seven years or so. He had left Hongkong for his native district in February of this year.

label: text
text:
Asked by His Lordship if the firm had a banking account or letter headings in which Chan Yuksan's interest in the business was referred to, witness said that there were no such things.
Mr. Wong Pui-tong, the trustee appointed by the court in the matter of the estate of the debtor firm, gave evidence that among

label: text
text: Evidence was given as to the borrowing of money by the debt-or on, the security of the firm whose chops he used on the borrowing notes.

label: text
text: His Lordship said that the issue had been proved to his satisfaction and he would make an order in accordance with the application.

label: paragraph_title
text: ALLEGED THEFTS.

label: paragraph_title
text: EUROPEANS CHARGE HOUSE COOLIE.

label: text
text: MISSING "VALUABLES.

label: text
text: A house coolie long wanted by the police authorities, at last fell in the trap yesterday afternoon, having been arrested at No.10 Albion Terrace, Kowloon Dock. He is charged with kureny under three charges.

label: text
text: Mr. A. Thompson, an engineer at the Tai Tam Tuk Reservoir, who is the first complainant, alleges that while the accused was in his employ, on October, 1924, the accused stole $350 from him, and then disappeared.

label: text
text: Mr. J. R. Haywood, solicitor, who is the second complainant, alleges that while the accused was in his services on February, 1924, the accused stole a silver cigarette case.

label: text
text: Mr. Haywood representing his mother-in-law., and third complainant, alleges that while his mother-in-law was living with him at Derrington House, Garden Road, during which period the defendant was in his employ, the latter stole from his mother-in-law a gold wrist watch.

label: text
text: The wrist watch and the cigarette case were found in the possession of the accused, and were duly identified by the complaints.

label: text
text: The case was remanded until next Tuesday.

label: text
text: TIME IN COURT CASE.

label: text
text: Many things happened in the course of half an hour yesterday morning.

label: text
text: While a caretaker of the Glass makers' Guild at Water Street left the premises at 11 o'clock and returned in just that time, a thief sneaked in and removed a wall clock and a large vase.

label: text
text: At the other end of the street, at 11:30 o'clock, a wary detective had caught a man stalking behind the stalls with a gunny sack containing the stolen articles.

label: text
text: All parties met at the Police Station and the clock pointed to 11.10, the time it was taken down from the wall.

label: text
text: The arrested man was charged before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning with breaking into the premises, but the probability being that the caretaker forgot to lock the door through which he entered, he was convicted only on unlawful possession.

label: text
text: His explanation was that he was employed to carry the bag for another man who disappeared when he was stopped by the detective. The sentence was four weeks' hard labour.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: TRIBUTE TO HEROISM.

label: text
text: The Naval Board of Inquiry into the cause of the explosion of Lake Denmark on July 11 conclude that the disaster was caused by lightning. They pay a tribute to the heroism displayed by the officers and men on the scene and recommend them for decorations.

label: text
text: The rebuilding of Lake Denmark is recommended, but not for high explosives. The construction of two new depots is advised near the Pacific Coast on the Gulf of Mexico. --Reuter's American Service.

label: text
text: Capt. R. C. Lewis, lately in command of the Chinese steamer "Derwent," and formerly in command of the two well-known coasters "Pheumpenh" and "Haldis," has left for Home, where he hopes to regain his health.

label: text
text: The many friends of Mrs. C. W. Dawson, widow of a former Hongkong public servant, will regret to hear that she is very seriously ill in Yorkshire, whither she went from Hongkong in March last. A cable advising her relatives was received yesterday and her sister, Miss Ruby Mow Fung, is leaving by the Delta on Saturday.

label: text
text: COXWAIN'S OFFENCE

label: text
text: There was an echo of the charge against the coxswain of the lighter 'Delaware' belonging to the Standard Oil Company in Hongkong, at the Kowloon Magistracy this morning. The coxswain was charged last week with stealing sixteen cases of tin plates, a part of an order coming from the States to the Company in Hongkong, and was sentenced to nine months' hard labour, upon conviction.

label: text
text: Mr. J. H. E., Ninth Magistrate, remarked that although the defence did not petition a rehearing of the case he was reopening it, because in reviewing the case he noticed that the section under which the charge was brought allowed a maximum sentence of six months dead labour

label: text
text: The convict's term was therefore reduced from nine months to six months hard labour.

label: paragraph_title
text: A WIFE'S DEBTS?

label: paragraph_title
text: CHINESE DENIES LEGAL LIABILITY.

label: text
text: CONFLICTING EVIDENCE.

label: text
text:
That the debts, if incurred at all, must have been incurred by his tim fong wife, since deceased, and as to whose affairs he was not concerned, was the defence in the Summary Court this morning of Wong Sham-chen, of 238. Queen's Road East.
Defendant was sued by Chau Chung, trading as Wing Fut, for $125.76, the claim being made up of an alleged loan and goods alleged to have been sold and delivered to defendant.

label: text
text:
Mr. D. McCallum was for plaintiff and Mr. M. K. Lo for defendant.
Mr. McCallum, at the outset, said shunt Mr. Lo had given him notice that with regard to the claim for goods sold and delivered be (Mr. Lo) was relying on the statutes of limitation which laid down that claims under $1,000 must be sued on within three years unless there had been payment on account of written terms to pay.

label: text
text:
Mr. McCallum indicated that he would have no reply to this and his claim was therefore reduced to $81.
Plaintiff gave evidence as to the loan which he maintained was to the defendant in person and called evidence as to the handing over of the money to the defendant. Witness denied that either, the goods or loan were handed to the defendant's wife.

label: text
text: Defendant's story, in the witness box, was a complete denial of any personal loan or of the receipt of goods. He maintained that they had been made to his tin fong wife, now dead, and that he was not responsible for them.

label: text
text: His Honour, Mr. Justice Wood, adjourned the case until Monday when it will be taken in conjunction with another action brought by the plaintiff against the defendant. Plaintiff claims damages for alleged breach of trust by the defendant as head of two money loan associations which had given up business.
